correctness.rationale: Uniform compositions are exactly fair cut strings. Conditioning on S=s makes the cut set a uniform s-subset; adding a uniformly chosen absent cut produces a uniform (s+1)-subset and can only shorten the longest zero run. The exact single-coordinate Bernoulli covariance gives the influence identity. For a unique longest run, the total decrement is at most floor((L+1)^2/4), and a union bound on run starts yields E(L+1)^2<=m^2+4m+6. Classical longest-run variance asymptotics then imply the correlation rate.

originality.rationale: The 1986 Bernoulli-run paper gives the exact conditional distribution of longest run given the number of successes, so that fact is treated as prior. The closest same-object composition paper from 2020 computes mixed moments numerically/recursively and explicitly leaves a rigorous proof of rho(N)->0 open. No inspected source states the influence identity or the resulting root-N polylogarithmic correlation bound.
residual_risks: The exact conditional distribution from 1986 could make stochastic monotonicity derivable by algebra even though it is not stated in the inspected text.
Older run-statistics literature may contain an unstated covariance estimate stronger than the searched formulations.
No matching lower asymptotic is proved, so the exact decay order of the covariance remains open.

value.rationale: Part count and largest part are canonical statistics of a uniform composition, and a later same-object study explicitly requested a rigorous proof of asymptotic decorrelation. The result gives a strong stochastic-regression statement, an interpretable coordinate-influence formula, and a quantitative rate sufficient to settle that qualitative question.
